Review number 2.

I have a review under an old account which highlights my initial poor experience with an incorrect part supplied (351 gasket for a 289 and argued that it couldn't be wrong even when it was going to leave an 0.5mm seal at the front of the head 🤔).

Now, come round 2, I have finally come to fitting a grill trim part for my 66 mustang that I bought off these guys and its quality is APPALLING!

Motowell brand from Taiwan. Not even Scott Drake.

The wire clips are so loose that they spin around trying to push them in, so you simply cant use them. I used the clips from the original trim and they're tight as. So I clipped it in, only to then find it is way too short so the centre join cover doesnt even cover the gap.

From my experience with these guys, it has been nothing short of an embarrassment on their behalf.

Seeing as last time they asked to the last detail of the images I took so they could hinge on the one I didnt take as their out...please see included photos of the difference in gap between their product (the short one) and the original that fits under an original metal FoMoCo stamped centre piece.

Absolutely will not be buying off these guys again. And Im surprised by their reviews, because obviously people have gotten on well. But for some reason they (Mark especially) couldn't have looked after me worse! Both product and service.

I would usually contact them before leaving a negative review but after the service I got last time I tried, I honestly am not even going to try. As I have noted in my other review, I love giving out 5 star reviews and I have worked in customer service so I know what grumpy customers are like. I am honest however and my experience with these guys has been a definite 1 star.

Bought some supposedly premium garden soil. When it was delivered it was 80% sand. Called to advise and sent photos. All apologies and admitted they had given me the wrong soil. Admitted they refunded my delivery fee. But my vegie seedlings have been dying ever since. Phoned to let them know and was told the owner would call me when they arrived on sight. Still waiting for that phone call. Feeling like I’m being ignored. And ripped off. At least have the guts and decency to ring and discuss the issue.

Thank you for your response. My recollection of the conversation is that the response was “ the best I can do is to offer you a refund on your delivery fee. I then asked if the soil would affect any vegies I planted. Your response was no. It won’t affect anything , it should be fine. But I suppose it depends on how things are remembered. I have since sought advise on how to improve the soil and have bought a heap of products from Bunnings.

one_star_reviews.text:
I went back to Hillsong for a second time, hoping the experience might be different, but unfortunately it reinforced my first impression.

Once again, the service felt heavily focused on pulling at people’s heartstrings to encourage them to give money. The first time, the message centred around “I still love the church”; this time, a large part of the focus was on sponsoring a child.

What disappointed me most was that I never felt like we were actually being taught from the Bible. There was no real opening up of Scripture, explaining what it means, or showing us something from the Bible that we could genuinely take away and put into practice in our everyday lives. To me, a church service should be centred around Jesus and teaching the Word, not fundraising.

I personally wouldn’t give Hillsong a cent. I also have concerns about how much money a large organisation like this generates and how much actually reaches those who need help. If I’m giving money to help people, I want to know that the majority of it is actually going toward helping them.

If you’re looking for a church on the Gold Coast where the focus feels more genuinely centred on faith, Scripture and community, I’d recommend checking out the old Surf City Church near Q1 (presence church) or Hope Church at Varsity Lakes. I’ve had a much better experience at both.

For me, Hillsong was a second chance, and I won’t be going back. I believe Jesus Himself warned about religious organisations that put money and appearances ahead of genuine faith and helping people

GoodLife, you ought to be ashamed of yourselves!!! I'm disgusted and glad I read the hidden terms & conditions before joining with my mentally & physically disabled cousin's refferal. Read up on this place & protect your loved ones....

This gym engages in deeply predatory contract traps and has zero empathy for its members. They locked my cousin, who as I stated, has both mental & physical disabilities, into a predatory 12-month contract over an iPad sign-up. She is currently experiencing severe financial hardship, and instead of showing basic human decency, GoodLife is ruthlessly exploiting her situation.

They are demanding a $225 cancellation fee on top of $300 in accumulated fees just to let her leave, all while slapping her with exorbitant late fees every single day to actively worsen her financial distress. Their policy only allows a single month to freeze a membership for free before forcing vulnerable people to pay just to keep it frozen, and absolutely none of these extreme financial penalties or contract traps were ever clearly explained or disclosed at sign-up.

To make matters worse, their customer service and management are appalling. They ignored emails and only called her once, completely inappropriately, four and a half hours after business hours during dinner time (who calls at 9:30PM?!?!). When she tried to explain her financial hardship and disability, the staff were incredibly passive-aggressive and told her she "might have to wait" for even a basic one-month freeze to be approved. Gross how they pretended to be friendly toward her and made her feel like a bad person for not paying them more money that she DOESN'T HAVE!!

On top of being financially predatory, the physical gym itself is completely neglected. It is consistently dirty, unhygienic, gross, and unfriendly. They pour all their energy into aggressive sales tactics and trapping people in contracts rather than maintaining a clean, functioning facility or training their staff in basic customer service. They are actively exploiting a vulnerable person with a disability for profit.

Save your money, protect your peace of mind, and go literally anywhere else. Count your days GoodLife Moolroobark, from reading other reviews it seems you've been doing this foolish nonsense for years.

Worst experience I’ve ever had at a medical centre.

I had been waiting three weeks for this appointment to get an iron infusion. After finally attending, I was made to wait for almost two hours, only for the doctors to be unable to find a suitable vein to insert the cannula and proceed with the infusion.

I completely understand that sometimes IV access can be difficult. However, after waiting three weeks and spending almost two hours at the medical centre, I was understandably frustrated that the treatment could not be provided.

What made the experience even worse was being charged $200, with only $150 refunded. I was effectively charged $50 for a service that was not completed.

When I tried to explain my concerns to the reception staff, instead of showing understanding or acknowledging the situation, I was met with a very rude and dismissive attitude. The response, “What are you after?”, was extremely inappropriate when I was simply trying to understand why I was being charged for an unsuccessful appointment.

I understand that medical procedures don’t always go as planned, but patients’ time, money and frustration should still be respected. After waiting three weeks for an appointment and spending two hours there without receiving the treatment, I expected much better communication, professionalism and customer service.

Very disappointing experience. I would not recommend this medical centre.

one_star_reviews.text:
**Important: I do not recommend seeing Dr Bindu Murali for Stage 4 deep infiltrating endometriosis, particularly with bowel involvement.**

I rarely leave negative reviews, but I feel it is important to share my experience to help others. Endometriosis is often underdiagnosed, and patients can face years of being dismissed. It took me 23 years to receive my diagnosis before recently relocating from the UK.

Following my MRI and specialist endometriosis scan, Dr Murali advised that surgery was too high-risk, that I would likely need a colostomy bag, and that surgery might not relieve my pain. She also dismissed my severe bowel symptoms as unrelated, suggesting I had a “lazy bowel" and my fatigue was psychological.
I left the appointment feeling devastated and without hope. The only treatment offered was the contraceptive pill, with no other pain management.

I recently consulted a specialist in Sydney who focuses on complex endometriosis, adenomyosis and bowel involvement. He took the time to listen, thoroughly understand my symptoms and explain how my bowel issues were definitely connected to my condition. I was also referred to a pain management specialist which should of been done previously. The difference in approach and knowledge was very noticeable.

I recognise that Dr Murali may be highly experienced in other areas of gynaecology; however, based on my experience, I do not believe she was the right specialist for my complex condition. I would have definitely appreciated greater transparency about the limits of her expertise "This is not my speciality" and a referral to a surgeon specialising in complex endometriosis and bowel surgery.

The repeated emphasis on the possibility of a colostomy was very distressing. I was advised today that this is a rare complication of the surgery being considered in my case, which reinforced my concerns about the advice I had received.

After 23 years of struggling to obtain a diagnosis and being repeatedly dismissed, this experience was extremely difficult. **I strongly encourage anyone with Stage 4 deep infiltrating endometriosis or bowel involvement to seek out a specialist with specific expertise in complex endometriosis surgery.**

I am relieved to have finally found a specialist in Sydney who listens, understands my condition and can discuss appropriate treatment options at the stage it has unfortunately got to.

My review is specifically about my experience with Psychologist, Sheleagh White, not the clinic as a whole. I saw her for approximately a year during one of the most difficult periods of my life, when my husband and I were experiencing serious problems.
Looking back, this was by far the least helpful experience I’ve had with any psychologist before or since. Rather than helping us communicate or de-escalate, I often left sessions feeling more divided, as if the conflict between us had been unintentionally reinforced.
I was also concerned by some of the advice and information I received. For example, I was told that if my child was not up-to-date with vaccinations, they would not be able to attend school. I later understood that this was not accurate at all after contacting different schools. She asked my husband to vaccinate my kids without my permission and I was so surprised when a significant parenting decision was encouraged without my agreement.

Another interaction that has stayed with me was being told, “You are a naughty girl,” because I had not read a recommended book. I found this language patronising and inappropriate in a professional setting.
What I found particularly frustrating was that a considerable amount of session time was spent discussing the psychologist’s own personal life and family. I frequently heard stories about her husband, daughter, mother, and other personal matters. I often left feeling I had spent more time listening than being listened to.
Therapy should be a place where clients feel heard, respected, and supported. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.
Everyone’s experience will be different, but based on mine, I cannot recommend this psychologist.

I called the North Ryde Fire Station and was told that two trucks attended Meadowbank Grove for a fire alarm on the night in question.

I don’t expect I’ll ever get an answer to my question.

I contacted Mercedes-Benz and asked them to check the sensor. I had already been charged for the sensor check. His behaviour escalated to the point where he made a fist and struck/put it forcefully on the table. I found this behaviour intimidating, aggressive and completely unacceptable in a customer service environment.
He then told me, “Don’t ever come here. Get out.” I was extremely disappointed and shocked by the way I was spoken to and treated.
I believe customers should be treated with respect, especially when there has been a misunderstanding regarding charges. If additional costs were going to apply, I should have been informed and given the opportunity to approve them beforehand, as was discussed.
I strongly believe the owner/management should review this incident and speak with Lucas about appropriate professional and respectful behaviour towards customers. In my opinion, this type of behaviour is not acceptable for someone working in customer service.
I have previously expected a high standard of service from Mercedes-Benz, but unfortunately this experience has left me very disappointed.

one_star_reviews.text:
For the past nine years, I have purchased three new pairs of glasses every year from Specsavers Parramatta and have generally been very happy with the experience. This year, I decided to give Oscar Wylee Parramatta a chance. Unfortunately, I regret that decision.
I had an eye test and then selected three different pairs of glasses, two for reading and one for long-distance driving. I paid an additional $420 out of pocket on top of what my health insurance covered.
After waiting around two weeks, I was notified that my glasses were ready for collection. When I tried them on, all three pairs were out of focus and blurry, making them difficult to see through.
I was then remeasured, including measurements of my facial dimensions and the positioning of the lenses. I was told that incorrect measurements had initially been taken, which apparently explained why the glasses were blurry. I was asked to wait another fortnight for the glasses to be remade.
When I returned, the long-distance driving glasses were finally okay. However, the reading glasses were still out of focus.
After a lot of back and forth, I had another eye test. I was then told that if I am looking at my computer screen from approximately 15cm away, I would require one type of glasses, whereas if I am looking at it from approximately 25cm away, I would require a different prescription.
I have never heard a load of nonsense, baloney, drivel, hogwash in all my life. I have been wearing glasses for many years and have never experienced anything like this. The explanation I received was extremely frustrating and, quite frankly, made little sense to me.
The biggest issue is that I have now paid an additional $420 for glasses that I cannot properly use. I have even included a photo of the glasses because, unfortunately, they have effectively become useless to me.
I gave Oscar Wylee an opportunity after nine years with Specsavers, and unfortunately the experience has been extremely disappointing. There were measurement errors, delays, multiple visits and still no satisfactory resolution for the reading glasses.
Specsavers Parramatta, I'm sorry. I should never have left you.
Based on my experience, I would not recommend Oscar Wylee Parramatta and I certainly won't be returning.

one_star_reviews.text:
When Michael called us to give us the diagnosis, which had initially been offered as a one-hour complimentary diagnosis, the call took place approximately six hours after I had dropped off the car. Fortunately, we didn’t need to use the car that day, so the delay itself was not an issue for us.

During the call, Michael offered us a complimentary engine wash and a complimentary wheel change. He also suggested that we drive the car for a week and then bring it back so he could re-check the engine and monitor the oil leak.

We had originally agreed to pay for the wheel change, but since Michael had offered it to us free of charge, we naturally expected this to be honoured. We called before going to pick up the car to confirm the arrangements, so we expected everything to have been communicated internally.

However, when my boyfriend arrived to collect the car, the receptionist told him, “The car has been here for two days and we didn’t know what we were supposed to do with it.” He tried to politely explain what Michael had offered us during our phone call, but the receptionist reacted in a very unpleasant manner.

What made the situation even more frustrating was that the car had already been there for more than a day, and the agreed engine wash and wheel change had not even been carried out. In the end, they only changed the wheel; the engine wash was not done.

We would also like to clarify something regarding the response to my boyfriend’s review mentioning that the diagnosis took 2.5 hours. We booked the car in based on a one-hour complimentary diagnosis, and at no point were we told that if the diagnosis took longer than one hour, we would be charged for the additional time. If this had been explained to us beforehand, we would have had the opportunity to decide whether we wanted to proceed with any additional work or charges.

Overall, Michael was great, but unfortunately the poor communication and attitude at reception made the overall experience much less positive than it could have been.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unethical and unprofessional agent – callous, manipulative and money-grabbing.

A few months after my father passed away, I contacted Lynda White to manage his deceased estate. She initially presented as kind, compassionate and generous with her time, saying she would “hold my hand” through managing my dad’s property and belongings while I navigated my grief. As this was my first experience with a rental property, I trusted her.

My dad had severe disability following a stroke and disability equipment worth over $20,000. At our first meeting, Lynda focused on having it donated to Shannon’s Bridge, a charity with which she had personal associations, rather than discussing her contract. Although I had not hired her, I felt pressured into agreeing. In hindsight, this demonstrated poor professional boundaries and steamrolled my decision-making over valuable property.

Lynda provided prospective tenant applications and strongly encouraged one. I noticed she had failed to obtain details for a second leaseholder. When I raised this, she initially said there was no second leaseholder, then realised this was untrue.

She also failed to arrange a second inspection after the first did not secure a tenant, waiting for me to request one. She sent a draft lease, explicitly saying she would add terms regarding care of the furniture and fixtures for my review. It never happened.

After the second inspection, I agreed to another application. The applicants wanted to start within a week. I assumed Lynda would provide the final lease for my approval before it was signed. Instead, tenants signed it less than 48 hours before commencement, without giving me the opportunity to review it or provide written authority. The final lease also omitted the agreed furniture/fixture terms, leaving me pressured to sign an agreement I was unhappy with.

Clause 11.3 of the Management Authority states that the agent may sign a Residential Rental Agreement on my behalf only after receiving my written request and authority, and that the agreement must contain terms agreed by the Rental Provider and Renter.

Lynda also failed to act on electrical and minimum standards reports sent to her on 4 August, identifying a required electrical repair. I only discovered this after following up with the auditor a week later, shortly before the tenants were due to move in. Being interstate, I arranged last-minute flights for my electrician partner, costing over $600. Lynda said that if I chose to arrange the inspections, following them up was my responsibility. I did not “choose” to take this task on; I had received no guidance about delegation, and subsequently learned that organising minimum standards reports is the property manager’s responsibility. Her failure caused unnecessary financial loss.

I then requested to terminate the management authority immediately, waiving the 90-day notice period because I believed her unauthorised conduct justified this. Lynda agreed to terminate immediately but said she would take her management fee for the 90-day period as an “exit fee”. This was the first I heard of such a fee, and no exit fee appears in the contract. Without specifying how it was calculated or payable, she unilaterally deducted $497 from the first rent payments. I have also not received the remaining rent monies into my nominated account, nor has she explained this. I have reported the matter to Consumer Affairs.

On 14 August, the day the tenancy commenced, Lynda instructed an agent named Chris, whom I had never met, to call me after business hours because she had suddenly gone on leave.

In summary, Lynda:
• breached clause 11.3 by allowing tenants to sign a lease without my prior written authority or approval and by omitting agreed terms;
• failed to act on an electrical/minimum standards report, causing over $600 in unnecessary costs;
• deducted $497 as an exit fee not provided for in the contract

STEER CLEAR IF YOU KNOW WHAT’S GOOD FOR YOU, AND FIND YOURSELF A PROFESSIONAL AND ETHICAL AGENCY.

one_star_reviews.text: Receptionist was incredibly rude and unhelpful, please listen to the reviews of this place, I wish I had before I came here

I was referred to Dr Remy Glowinski at Brighton Minds.
After waiting 6 weeks for my first appointment I was turned away as I was some 7’ minutes late. I left in tears. After seeing my distress the receptionist implored me to come back and scheduled me in for the following week. After a number of sessions with Dr Glowinski , and after downloading my life story he advised that he would no longer see me and referred me to someone else in the clinic he felt better equipped. During my sessions with him Dr Glowinski was cold and almost clinical in his approach to my situation. He questioned certain details that I shared, disturbingly asking me for the finer details , almost questioning the legitimacy of it all. I left exhausted, distressed and disappointed but made new appointment with his colleague as suggested. Over the coming week I went over and over our discussions during my sessions with him and it suddenly occurred to me that he had lost, or perhaps never possessed the most important human trait, something imperative for a practicing psychiatrist, HUMILITY.
I feel Dr Glowinski is only interested in treating your simple garden variety of cases,  and if too much work for him he simply closes his door.
An awful and traumatic experience here, if you need help I definitely do not recommend seeing him.

I was repeatedly passed between different people and was later told that the phone number I had called was a personal number, despite that number being publicly listed on the company’s website. The email address I used was also the contact email provided on their website.

Overall, I found the entire process unnecessarily difficult and poorly handled. I followed the contact process I was specifically instructed to use, made several genuine attempts to obtain pricing, and was ultimately left with a very poor impression of the company’s communication and customer service.

⭐ 1 STAR But I would give negative 5 stars if I could!!

My experience with Plan Partners has been absolutely atrocious.

For months I have been trying to resolve unpaid invoices, and what should have been a straightforward matter has turned into an exhausting battle of unanswered emails, repeated phone calls, constantly changing requirements and excuse after excuse.

I have now called Plan Partners more than 20 times trying to resolve this matter. I have sent numerous emails, repeatedly provided information requested of me and contacted their complaints department on multiple occasions.

Despite all of this, the matter remains unresolved.

One of the most frustrating aspects has been the constant shifting of the goalposts. Each time I address one issue or provide information requested, another reason seems to appear as to why payment cannot be made.

I have repeatedly requested that Plan Partners provide me with the actual written documentation, policy or guidelines setting out exactly what is required for an invoice to be approved. Instead of receiving this, I have continued to receive more questions and changing explanations. They refuse to provide any documentation what so ever! They even refuse to provide a direct email or contact number to lodge a formal complaint.

Numerous emails have gone unanswered. Phone calls have resulted in being passed around or told to email yet again. Even escalating the matter through their complaints process has failed to produce a satisfactory resolution although I firmly believe they don’t have an escalations department and their front desk staff simply pretend to be an escalation point!

Meanwhile, 5 months of invoices totaling thousands has gone unpaid!

I am now taking legal action to recover the money owed and pursuing the formal complaint avenues available to me.

No individual or small business should have to make more than 20 phone calls and spend months chasing payment while continually being given different reasons for why an invoice will not be paid.

I noticed that they tell ALL their 1 star reviews to email them to resolve issues yet they don’t respond to their emails or on the rare occasion when they do, they give a generic response rather than address and questions or concerns you have.

The amount of time, stress and frustration this has caused is completely unacceptable.

Based solely on my own experience, I would never recommend Plan Partners. If you have any financial dealings with this company, document absolutely everything, insist on requirements being provided to you in writing and keep records of every email and phone call.

I do not experience these issues with any of the other providers that I work with.

I wish I had known what dealing with Plan Partners would be like before this began. As a small business, I cannot afford the wasted time I have spent trying to resolve this with plan partners. They are unethical and I am now refusing to take on any client that would involve me having to deal with plan partners!

Plan Partners have no idea what they are doing half the time they don't even have the right up to date funds of the plan of multiple clients. Multiple invoices and service agreements knocked back because they don't have the right data even when informed by the participants. I had a client show they rejected codes under plan managed that were normally cleared when the client was ndis managed. They incorrectly flag providers for overbilling because they have no idea how to read a budget breakdown of remaining funds and plan end dates. one_star_reviews.text:
Please look at the photo. This is Jetstar's service ‼️‼️

I booked a tour, hotel, and flights as a package through Booking.com, and it clearly stated that up to 20 kg of checked baggage was included free of charge. However, when I asked the ground staff at the airport on the day of departure, I was told that this information had not been reflected in their system. In the end, I was charged $170 × 2 = $340 for two pieces of luggage, even though the total weight was within the 20 kg limit.
I intend to claim this charge from Booking.com later (￣^￣)

I flew with Jetstar NZ from New Zealand to Brisbane, Australia, and then took a connecting flight to Japan. First of all, the flight departing New Zealand was one hour late.

Throughout the entire flight, the cabin crew were unfriendly and provided virtually no service. Not a single one of them smiled, and instead of doing anything for passengers, they mostly stood in the galley chatting with each other, except when they came around to sell food.

Even water costs money. One bottle of water was $5.

I ordered the teriyaki vegetable noodles for $15, but they were so tasteless that I honestly wondered if I was eating rubber instead of noodles. They were absolutely terrible. Even after adding salt and pepper, there was virtually no teriyaki flavor at all. Paying $15 for something this awful was honestly ridiculous.

I really regret not buying a proper breakfast in New Zealand before the flight.

The cabin crew repeatedly bumped into my shoulder, hands, legs, etc. with the service cart and even with their own bodies, despite the fact that I wasn't even sticking out beyond the armrest. They never said a single word or apologized. Is their sense of balance seriously that bad?

I was also shocked to see a passenger sitting diagonally behind us being made to pick up trash from the floor and throw it away. I know it's a low-cost airline, but honestly, I thought the cabin crew were an absolutely crazy bunch—almost on the level of Cebu Pacific.

On top of that, the toilet paper wasn't replenished whenever I went to the restroom, and the Wi-Fi never worked even once. The USB port was apparently so small that it only accepted USB-C, so on a 10-hour flight there was no entertainment screen, I couldn't charge my devices, and there was basically nothing to do. It was seriously awful.

And then there was another unbelievable problem!!

I traveled from Auckland to Brisbane and then connected onward to Japan. When I arrived in Japan and went to collect my checked baggage, my suitcase wasn't there.

I've flown with Japanese low-cost airlines once or twice before, and I've never had my baggage fail to arrive. But this time, it wasn't just our suitcases. We found out that around 15 other passengers were also missing their luggage.

What kind of ridiculously careless baggage management is Jetstar running?

After arriving in Japan, I had to fill out a delayed/missing baggage report, which took even more time‼︎

Jetstar Japan is planning to transition to a new brand and is reportedly expected to announce the new brand as early as October. However, I think it should also reconsider its services.
Rather than simply launching a new brand, I would like the company to retrain its cabin crew in customer service and raise the overall standard of service.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with the way I was spoken to when I called Shalom House today to enquire about their rehabilitation program on behalf of a family member who was considering entering the program.

Before calling, I had already visited the Shalom House website and read through the information provided about the program and its different stages. However, from the beginning of the phone call, the man I spoke with came across as dismissive, sarcastic and unnecessarily confrontational. Rather than simply answering reasonable questions from a concerned family member, he repeatedly questioned me about whether I had read the website and appeared to expect me to recall every detail of a lengthy, multi-stage program after reading it once.

When I asked direct questions, I frequently received another question in response rather than a clear answer. This made what should have been a straightforward enquiry feel unnecessarily hostile and evasive.

One particular concern I wanted clarification about was the practice of cutting participants' hair, which I had previously heard about. When I asked why this was done, instead of simply explaining the policy and reasoning behind it, I was asked whether I had ever been to jail and was then questioned about what people do in jail. I explained that I had not been to jail and asked what that had to do with my question. The conversation then moved into explanations about multicultural backgrounds and other matters, but I still did not receive a clear answer as to why participants' hair is cut.

When I continued to respectfully ask for a direct answer, the call was ultimately ended without my question being answered and without any professional or courteous conclusion to the conversation.

What concerned me most is that Shalom House presents itself as a faith-based rehabilitation program. When families are considering placing someone they care about into a rehabilitation facility, they should be able to ask questions about the program, its rules and its practices without being treated as though those questions are an inconvenience or a challenge to authority. Transparency, patience, compassion and professionalism should be especially important in an environment dealing with vulnerable people and their families.

Based solely on my experience during this phone call, I was left with serious concerns about the culture and approach of the program. The interaction felt unnecessarily authoritarian and dismissive rather than supportive, compassionate or professional.

After this experience, I personally would not feel comfortable recommending Shalom House to any friends or family members. It does not seem like a safe place to entrust them with your loved ones

After this experience from just one phone call, I can only imagine what dealing with this kind of attitude over a period of several months could be like. I personally would not feel comfortable recommending Shalom House to any friends or family members. The manner in which my reasonable questions were handled raised serious concerns for me about whether I could confidently entrust the care of a vulnerable loved one to this program. If this is how a concerned family member is treated simply for asking reasonable questions before admission, it leaves me deeply concerned about how participants may be treated once they are inside the program.

⭐️ 1 star

Honestly, my experience with Alive Church Bundaberg was horrible.

I found Pastor Joey to be incredibly rude, ignorant and dismissive. What really stood out to me was how differently I felt I was treated depending on whether I was doing something for the church. When I was helping out and being useful, I felt welcomed and appreciated. The moment I needed to take a break or step away for a while, it felt like I suddenly didn’t matter anymore. I could barely get acknowledgment or a conversation.

That kind of behaviour is extremely disappointing from church leadership. People shouldn’t feel like they’re only valued when they’re doing something useful for the church.

The constant focus on money and giving during services was also a major negative for me. It became uncomfortable, and I felt there was pressure and guilt placed on people who weren’t giving. Church shouldn’t feel like you’re being constantly reminded that you need to contribute financially.

There are some genuinely nice people there, and I will give credit to the people who actually make an effort to come and talk to others. Unfortunately, I can’t say the same about the pastors. I felt like they would go out of their way to avoid me rather than simply treating me like a person and asking how I was doing.

Overall, I felt that respect and attention depended on where you stood within the church and how useful or involved you were. If you’re not part of the “inner circle,” my experience was that you can feel completely ignored.

For me, a church should be a place where people feel welcomed and valued regardless of what they can do, how much they give, or who they know. That’s not how I felt here, and I wouldn’t recommend it based on my experience.

I’ve shopped here many times and usually received good service, so today was disappointing. I asked the attendant what a beer I hadn’t tried was like. His response was, “It’s cold and wet,” followed by, “It tastes like beer.” When I asked whether it was sweet or fruity, I eventually got a helpful answer.
The sarcastic comments continued as I left, which made the whole interaction feel unnecessarily rude and dismissive. I like supporting local businesses, but basic courtesy goes a long way. Unfortunately, I’ll be shopping elsewhere in future.

This centre left me in a far worse place than when I started.   In reality it is my belief from my experience  that it is merely just hypnosis - cradled in a fancy set of pretty diagrams and big words .  These services are accessible only by signing up to the most unfair of terms and conditions completely one sided and what might be considered exorbitant in view of what is offered .

If you fail “the assessment” - the first session - after mandatory sign up for minimum 10 sessions at $340 plus $6 card fee on top - and waiting months - they reject you and it is even up to you to cancel the remaining 9 sessions to avoid more obligatory fees. You must agree upfront beforehand to be charged $100 - no exceptions - (I checked with them) if you don’t give them THREE BUSINESS days notice of cancellation beforehand - very unfair terms for people who have chronic health problems.  They charge your card without even notifying you they are going to do so. It is very difficult to get proper information about what the sessions actually cover - the staff in office tell you they don’t know but just “book your ten sessions show up to first one and Jim is so wonderful he will tell you everything you need.”

I found the psychologistt Jim to be extremely prickly and showed an arrogance accompanied by an alarming lack of understanding and compassion for people with mental health problems that often accompany people with chronic health problems in this field.

Due to my experience I belive  the “in person” assessment (you pay for) is to see if you are easy to hypnotise.  After a fairly unpleasant one hour session in which I bared my soul about childhood issues and a long difficult health journey after an hour he simply concluded “I don’t DO people with (my condition).”

When I queried him as to why he could not just prescreen by looking at the clearly ascertainable facts already provided to him months previously in the referral (which he read from in the session) which already clearly showed that I had that condition - he insinuated certain things which greatly upset me and left me feeling more vulnerable and hopeless than ever.  But he did undertake to find a number for someone else.  I rang the office and they were apologetic but just said something along the lines “well we just expect the referring doctor to GET what it is we actually do” which more or less confirmed my suspicions about them being quite vague about services provided and why after they have your doctor referral with all the details months before they dont bother to prescreen and you need to pay $340 for first session. This is all after you have to go to GP and also incur charges to get a health plan assigning all sessions to the gut centre beforehand

My suggestion would be if you think hypnosis is likely to help you just see a local psychologist trained in hypnotherapy on reasonable terms. Don’t be fodder for this lazy predatory firm who want you to take all the risks and costs in order to maximise their fees.

The biggest issue, however, was her phone which completely ruined any chance of relaxing. She also received several phone calls and messages during the session, with Siri reading her messages aloud so that their contents could be heard. At no point did she apologise or acknowledge any of these interruptions.

She also never checked in throughout the massage regarding pressure or comfort.

What should have been a relaxing and enjoyable experience instead became incredibly frustrating, distracting and I was unable to properly relax at all.

We’ve had positive experiences at other City Cave locations, so this was particularly disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
We chose this mechanic based on numerous positive recommendations from local people. We had only moved into the area about a year ago and weren’t familiar with the local businesses, so we trusted those recommendations.

Whilst the staff were friendly and helpful, and we booked in a service quickly, and received a text message reminder, unfortunately the rest of our experience was extremely disappointing.

We spent approximately $3,500 on servicing and repairs, and unfortunately, our car was arguably in a worse condition when we collected it than when we dropped it off.

The most serious issue was the serpentine belt, which was not fitted correctly. The company subsequently acknowledged that they had not installed it properly. Within 15 minutes of collecting the car, the belt broke, leaving us stranded with two young children, no working car and no way of getting home. By the time this happened, the business was already closed.

When the belt broke, coolant bubbled over and sprayed throughout the engine bay and all over the car. The car was not cleaned afterwards, leaving us to deal with the mess ourselves.

There were also several other issues that we discovered:

• The brakes had been replaced, but the brakes had not been bled, meaning we had to return and specifically ask for this to be done.

• A new pollen filter had been fitted, but the leaves and debris had not been removed beforehand, resulting in a terrible noise from the ventilation system. We ultimately had to sort this out ourselves.

The whole situation resulted in an enormous amount of wasted time, inconvenience and stress. We were left without a usable car for two days, and despite the seriousness of what had happened, there was no meaningful apology, no offer of a hire car while our vehicle was being repaired, and no offer of compensation or assistance for the considerable inconvenience caused.

To be fair, they did provide free towing under their warranty/roadside assistance, which I appreciate. However, this still meant taking a day off work to wait for the tow truck and dealing with the consequences of a problem that should never have occurred in the first place.

What has been most disappointing is that after spending $3,500 and trusting the recommendations of local people, we were left feeling that there was very little accountability for the situation.

I understand that mistakes can happen in any business. What matters is how those mistakes are handled. In our case, the lack of proper care, communication and genuine accountability has left us extremely disappointed.

Unfortunately, based on our experience, we cannot recommend this business.

one_star_reviews.text:
One of the most stressful and extremely disappointing experiences.

The customer service and communication are absolutely terrible. It is incredibly difficult to get a clear or accurate answer to even a simple question, and I have been given incorrect information on more than one occasion. Calls are rarely returned after waiting in a queue for hours, emails and online enquiries can take an unreasonable amount of time to receive a response, and submitting an online enquiry often feels like it goes nowhere.

You are constantly told that someone will get back to you, but then nobody does. You end up having to repeatedly call, follow up and chase things yourself just to get basic information or have an enquiry properly addressed. Even when you do manage to speak to someone, you can be given conflicting information or passed between different people without anyone actually taking responsibility for resolving the issue. For a mental health service, this level of poor communication and lack of follow-through is particularly frustrating and stressful.

I also want to warn anyone considering using this service to be mindful of the experiences they may encounter with the doctors. I have found the level of empathy, understanding and compassion to be seriously lacking, which is particularly concerning in a field where patients are often in vulnerable positions and seeking support. Communication can come across as dismissive, and there seems to be a lack of consideration for how these interactions affect patients who are already struggling.

Psychiatric care should involve listening to patients, treating them with respect and making them feel heard and understood. Unfortunately, that level of care has been lacking in my experience, and it can leave patients feeling even more distressed, invalidated and unsupported than they were before seeking help

I have also found the opinions and recommendations provided through the service difficult to navigate at times, as they have not always felt consistent. When you are already trying to navigate your mental health and understand what treatment is appropriate for you, receiving differing opinions without clear communication can make an already difficult process even more confusing and stressful.

Seeking psychiatric support can already be a difficult and vulnerable experience. The process should make patients feel supported and understood, not leave them feeling like they have to constantly advocate for themselves just to receive a response or have their concerns taken seriously.

Overall, I think there needs to be significant improvement in both customer service and the way patients are treated. Empathy, clear communication, reliability and continuity of care should be fundamental to mental healthcare.

I’m sharing this because I wish I had seen more detailed reviews describing these issues before using the service. After reading many of the other reviews, I was genuinely surprised by how many people appear to have experienced similar problems with communication and patient care. I hope this review helps someone make a more informed decision before choosing this service.

I was booked in to see Dr James Heaney this morning after waiting five weeks for my appointment. I had rearranged my work week to make sure I was available and on time, only for him not to attend.

After waiting in the chat for 30 minutes with no update, I had to contact customer service myself. They contacted him and told me he was unavailable and that the appointment would need to be rescheduled.

Considering the cost of these appointments and the sensitive nature of the care being sought, I would expect, at the very least, to be notified if a doctor cannot attend. The lack of communication and consideration for my time and wellbeing was extremely disappointing by Dr James Heaney.

one_star_reviews.text:
We recently engaged with Jellis Craig Moonee Valley to sell our property, and appointed two of their agents whom we’d  previously worked with and knew. A week into the campaign both agents left. We were told not to worry, and that a managing director from Jellis Craig Kensington would take over the campaign and conduct the auction. However, this was not to be the case. Two days prior to auction, we were informed that he had another auction on the same day, at the same time and would no longer be available to conduct ours.
An independent auctioneer was brought in at the last minute. We’d made our preferences clear that we did not want the bidding to start excessively low. Despite this, the auctioneer opened the bidding significantly below the level we had indicated. Which we felt gave prospective buyers a misleading impression of the price expectations for the property. And the property passed in nowhere near our reserve.

After the auction, we felt pressured to accept an offer well below our reserve from our representing agent. Despite making it clear we were not willing to sell for that amount.
We were told that’s all it was worth, despite comparable sales suggesting otherwise.
While we are pleased we were ultimately able to achieve a sale, the final result doesn’t change how poorly we felt looked after throughout the campaign.

Unfortunately, this wasn’t an isolated experience. We had previously experienced a number of issues with Jellis Craig in relation to another rental property, which also left us disappointed with the level of service and support we received.
We had a tenant break their 12-month lease within the first three months and leave the property in poor condition, including multiple damages to the property. We were advised by Jellis Craig to allow the tenant to leave which left us with the cost of repairs and four months without a tenant, resulting in a significant loss of rental income and cost of damages.
We also experienced difficulty getting the property re-tenanted. When we raised these concerns with Jellis Craig on a number of occasions, we felt they we were brushed aside and we were essentially told that the matter was out of their hands and was now a VCAT issue. Throughout the situation, we felt we weren’t adequately supported or represented as the property owners.

Overall, our experience with Jellis Craig has been disappointing, across both property management and the sale of our property. Selling a property is a major decision, and we expected a much higher level of professionalism, communication and commitment. Based on our overall experience, we would not use them again and would be very hesitant to recommend them to others.

I debated writing this.... But it needs to be said.

I was referred here nearly two years ago to see a psychiatrist after not being able to get help through the public sector and I was very mentally unwell.

After 3 sessions I was diagnosed with possible bipolar disorder and put on medication which seemed to help for about a year.
It was also pushed on me to do day sessions at an extra cost (a seperate program they run), I initially agreed and than cancelled as I didn't need it.

Fast forward late last year I needed a medication review due to a few episodes and the same psychiatrist agreed to see me...

In my appointment she was very passive aggressive, then told me she didn't think I had bipolar anymore due to the medication now needing adjusting! She then passively aggressively said that I clearly didn't agree with her! She then charged me over $300 for 15 minutes.
She then AGAIN tried to push the program onto me several times which I declined.

Furthermore the report she sent my doctor was insulting! She supposedly made some untrue observations about my life, which weren't true and then she just added in a few diagnosis that I could or couldn't have .... All that in 15 minutes?!

This will now be permanently in my medical records. Which is unacceptable.

Absolutely unprofessional and vile treatment, I will not be back and I suggest people stay clear of this place.

one_star_reviews.text:
Your employee repeatedly called me a “dickhead” after damaging my car, then told me “Welcome to Australia”, “You can’t drive”, “It’s a joke” and “I’m loving it”.

This was not a simple disagreement over a minor scratch. Your employee initially attempted to leave the scene without properly exchanging information. When I insisted on exchanging the necessary details, he became increasingly hostile and continued verbally abusing, insulting and mocking me in a public car park. The entire incident lasted approximately 20 minutes.

Police were eventually called to attend and deal with the incident. When police asked your employee to provide his driver’s licence, he stated that he had an international driver’s licence.

I also found it concerning that, during the incident, your employee complained to me that he works 78 hours a week and was smoking at a petrol station. I cannot verify whether the 78-hour figure is accurate, but I believe Skyworld should consider whether appropriate fatigue management and employee wellbeing measures are in place.

I formally complained to Skyworld and gave the company a reasonable opportunity to address the employee’s conduct. However, I was left with the impression that the priority was to shut down the complaint rather than properly address the issue. I was not asking for details of any internal disciplinary process or outcome. I simply asked for a formal apology and an acknowledgement that the behaviour was inappropriate. I have retained relevant evidence relating to the incident and the employee’s conduct.

I have now been waiting 38 days for an apology, and my question to Skyworld remains simple: Does this behaviour align with Skyworld’s values and standards of conduct?

Many thanks to the reception, she was patient and listening, I sincerely appreciate your help and transferring the information.

Incredibly poor business ethics and completely misleading billing.
I signed up for the Kickstart Program ($198/month) at the Sunshine Coast clinic. This week, we found out their only local GP left the company, meaning they can no longer provide the face-to-face medical care we signed up for. Because they failed to provide the service, we called to cancel.
On Wednesday, the clinic explicitly assured us over the phone that the membership was cancelled with a $0 balance. On Thursday, they completely reneged on their word, locked our account, and demanded an extra $198 fee, falsely claiming we "owed" money for a dietitian appointment—even though we have only used a fraction of the package we already paid for.
Charging penalty fees when the clinic itself can no longer provide a doctor is completely unacceptable and breaches Australian Consumer Law. A formal complaint is being lodged with the Office of Fair Trading Queensland. Avoid this company—their administrative and billing practices are a nightmare.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unbelievable building experience with Plantation Homes.

1. Timber frame exposed to water
When the timber frame was sitting in water, my concern was that appropriate steps should have been taken to protect the timber and prevent moisture and mould issues. Instead of addressing my concerns about the condition of the timber, Travis criticised me for reporting the issue via email to Plantation Homes. Travis and their team also repeatedly told us that the timber was not mouldy and that everything was fine. Based on those assurances, I proceeded with payment for the timber frame stage.

2. The mould remediation plan
The original mould remediation plan was discussed and developed with the first mould treatment company, manager D, supervisor K and ourselves. The first mould treatment company recommended a number of treatments, including fogging treatment, solution treatment and the use of dehumidifiers. Travis later told us that Plantation Homes would use a second mould treatment company, Mouldmen, and assured us that they would carry out the same method of treatment as the first company, but at a lower cost. Based on this information, I agreed to proceed with the second company in order to help reduce Plantation Homes' costs.
We were also repeatedly told that the house needed to be enclosed before the mould remediation could proceed, Travis and Daniel continued pushing for the house to be enclosed so the treatment could proceed. However, on the day the mould treatment was carried out, the upper area of the house was not enclosed, and as a result, the fogging treatment did not go ahead. The Mouldmen specialist informed us in person on the scheduled treatment day that the fogging treatment could not proceed because the upper area of the house was still open. It appears that Travis did not expect us to have spoken directly with the Mouldmen specialist. Travis seemed to believe that we would not know that the fogging treatment had not gone ahead. It was only after we raised this issue directly with Travis that the matter was acknowledged.

Rather than arranging another appointment for the fogging treatment to be completed, Travis immediately changed his position and said that fogging treatment was no longer required.

When we requested writen confirmation or evidence directly from Mouldmen regarding whether the fogging treatment was required, Travis became angry during the phone conversation. He said words to the effect of, “Daniel and I have had enough of you. You don't tell me what to do,” and then hung up the phone.

The initial mould remediation plan was recommended by the first mould remediation company engaged by Plantation Homes themselves. We were advised that this was the appropriate industry best-practice approach for treating the mould by plantation homes.
However, on the day the mould treatment was scheduled, the upper area of the house had not been properly enclosed by their mistakes. After this issue was identified, Travis immediately changed his position and claimed that fogging treatment was not required.

This is extremely difficult to accept, particularly when the original remediation plan had been recommended by the mould specialist engaged by Plantation Homes.
In my experience, instead of taking responsibility for mistakes and ensuring the mould was properly treated, explanations kept changing after problems were identified.

Travis also threatened us with interest charges if we did not pay the enclosed stage invoice within 14 days, despite the fact that the agreed conditions relating to the mould remediation had not been met.
Trust me, based on my personal experience, I would strongly recommend staying away from them if you value your financial and general wellbeing. Make sure you carefully consider how construction issues, communication, and disputes are handled before choosing a builder.

I choose just cuts because of the atmosphere and kind professional service I have previously received but after this I will not be returning to this store.

I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding an interaction I had at Sale Post Office at approximately 12:30pm today.

I entered the post office to send a parcel and politely asked a staff member if I could have a piece of paper. I was more than happy to pay for it if necessary. Instead of simply answering my request, the staff member turned to another employee and said, “What do you reckon, should we give her a piece of paper?”

I found this extremely disrespectful and humiliating. I was polite to the staff member and was making a completely reasonable customer request, yet I was spoken about as though I was an inconvenience or someone deserving of ridicule. I subsequently felt so uncomfortable that I simply walked out without sending my parcel.

I am also particularly concerned that I was referred to as “her.” I am a man, and I have a beard and a masculine voice, so being deliberately referred to as female in this context was extremely inappropriate and felt targeted. Whether this was intended as a comment about my gender, my appearance, or something else entirely, it was completely unacceptable customer service.

Regardless of a customer's gender, appearance, personality, or whether they experience anxiety, customers should be treated with basic dignity and respect. Staff should not be making disparaging or mocking comments about customers to one another, particularly while the customer is standing directly in front of them.

I am absolutely appalled by the way I was treated and would like Australia Post to investigate this incident and address the behaviour with the staff involved. I would also strongly encourage Sale Post Office to ensure that all staff receive appropriate training on respectful, inclusive and professional customer service.

I do not expect special treatment. I simply expect to be treated with the same basic respect as any other customer.

I would appreciate a response regarding how this complaint will be addressed.

⭐️ 1/5 — Extremely disappointing experience with Interparcel

I paid $66 to have my package delivered, but the delivery failed. The most frustrating part is that I was not properly informed about the problem, even though Interparcel had both my phone number and email address.

I only discovered that there was an issue myself. Customer service then told me that I should simply check the tracking number to follow the shipment. I strongly disagree with this approach. If there is a problem with a delivery, customers should be properly informed, especially when their contact details have been provided for this exact purpose.

But the situation gets even worse.

Now, because the delivery was not completed, I am being told that I have to pay an additional $209 just to recover my own package.

So I paid $66 for a delivery service that was not successfully completed, I was not properly informed about the problem, and now I am apparently expected to pay another $209 to get my own property back.

This is completely unacceptable to me.

I have kept screenshots of all my conversations with customer service and all the relevant information regarding this shipment.

I am asking Interparcel to return my package to the Perth depot where I originally dropped it off, without charging me an additional $209.

I paid for a delivery service. I should not have to pay more than three times the original shipping cost simply to recover my own package after the delivery service failed.

Very disappointing experience. I would strongly recommend keeping screenshots and records of everything when using this company.

one_star_reviews.text:
I left the church one year ago but I decided my experience is worth sharing. I don’t mean to portray a negative view of Christianity as I’ve recently been to other churches with a positive experience and loving community. I’m not asking for compensation or communication from the pastors. I just want to share my experience.

The young adults and the leaders didn’t reflect God’s values as I expected. I joined the church before needing to temporarily move regionally. To formally join a cell group and join the group chat means being interrogated by your leaders and needing to serve at the church. They said in my interview ‘it’s not the season’ for me to join, and made an excuse like they don’t know how to support me living regionally. I wanted support in my new life chapter but ended up felt more isolated than I already was.

I also travelled three hours in Friday evenings (half a tank of fuel) on dark regional pothole highways to join the group just to feel ignored by majority of the cell group members. When I shared something personal and vulnerable to the group, my leader or one of the members would laugh instead of empathise, which was very hurtful. At one cell group social, I haven’t seen my leader for a few weeks and she didn’t even ask me how I have been. When other members came, she proceeded to talk to them instead and I felt very alone.

The final straw was when one of the members asked me a very judgemental rude personal question in front of the entire group in a public space and I felt so upset and humiliated. When I confronted her, I didn’t receive a genuine apology. This was when I knew I never wanted to return to this church again. No one (except for one member) followed up with me about my departure from the church, showing they probably never even cared about me in the first place.

I have expressed to the leaders and members that what they did upset me but there is a lack of accountability as they would say things like ‘we were just trying to get to know you’ or ‘we weren’t intending to upset you’ instead of admitting that what they did was inappropriate.

Additionally, the person who welcomed me and link me up with the church when I first came to the church appeared to ignore my partner and I for the rest of our time there, which I found gave a bad impression.

As a result, the entire experience was extremely toxic and brought me much pain and trauma.

I recommend if you’re looking for a church to attend, to find another church with a warm welcoming and loving community ❤️

one_star_reviews.text:
A deeply distressing experience — serious concerns about communication, money and dignity

I am writing this review following my family’s deeply upsetting experience with Elysian Fields Funerals in Bethania, following the passing of my brother.
At a time when our family was grieving and placing our trust in a funeral director to treat our loved one with dignity and respect, we were left with serious concerns about the services provided, the money paid and the lack of communication.
One of the most distressing things for our family was seeing tie-down straps placed over my brother’s coffin on a Harley-Davidson hearse, with towels also being used. This was heartbreaking to witness, and it was not the respectful presentation we expected for our loved one.
We also have serious concerns regarding the death certificate application. My understanding is that Anthony told my mother directly that he had applied for the death certificate, but we have reason to believe this was not done as represented. This is an extremely serious concern, particularly when families are relying on a funeral director to handle essential paperwork honestly and professionally.
There are also concerns about the money we paid for services and documentation. My brother’s cremation had already taken place before his funeral on 20 August 2026, yet we paid for a cremation certificate dated 17 August 2026. We have questions about exactly what was provided, what we were charged for and whether all the services paid for were properly fulfilled.
The lack of communication has only added to our distress. Families should not have to chase answers or be left questioning whether important arrangements and paperwork have been dealt with as promised.
Funeral directors are entrusted with caring for people at one of the most vulnerable times in their lives. That responsibility requires compassion, transparency, honesty and respect, both for the deceased and for the family left behind.
Losing my brother was painful enough without these additional concerns. Our family deserves clear answers and accountability regarding the money paid, the paperwork and the services we were promised.
I am sharing our experience so other families know to ask questions, obtain written confirmation of arrangements, keep all receipts and independently verify that important documentation has been completed.
Every family deserves honesty, transparency and dignity when saying goodbye to someone they love.

Extremely Disappointing – Would Not Recommend

After 20 years working in property management, I am appalled by how this agency has handled our tenancy and bond.

We spent over $1,500 on professional cleaning and gardening at vacate, yet the agent still disputed our exit. Our bond was $3,360 and the agent has confirmed in writing that only $542 is disputed. We have agreed for the full $542 to remain with the RTA, yet the agent has refused our request to facilitate release of the undisputed balance.

This comes after years of being cooperative tenants while maintenance requests were ignored or delayed, including mould concerns and an oven that was not properly repaired for approximately 2.5 years, while our rent continued to increase. The owner also refused pest control.

Our tenancy ended due to DFV, requiring an urgent interstate relocation. The lack of professionalism, reasonableness and compassion shown during an already difficult situation has been disgraceful.

After two decades in this industry, I know how tenants should be treated. I would never have handled a tenancy this way and as an previous owner i would never feel comfortable allowing a property manager to behave this way to my tenants

Everything is documented and the matter is proceeding through the appropriate channels.

Absolutely would not recommend this agency.

- REPLY TO OWNER REVIEW
Thank you for your response, however it does not address the actual issue raised in my review.

I am not objecting to your right to dispute $542. I have repeatedly agreed for the entire $542 to remain with the RTA and be independently determined.

Regarding the garden, I obtained evidence from two separate contractors stating that there was no pet damage and that no further garden works were required. Despite this evidence, you continued to pursue the garden/pet damage claim. I am more than happy for the RTA to consider the evidence from both sides and determine that dispute.

My primary concern remains that, out of our $3,360 bond, you have confirmed in writing that only $542 is disputed, yet you have refused our request to facilitate release of the remaining undisputed balance.

After 20 years working in property management, I understand how genuine bond disputes work. Please do not portray my complaint as being simply about having to pay for alleged pet damage. I dispute that damage and have contractor evidence supporting my position.

Everything stated in my review is supported by documentation, photographs, invoices and written correspondence and will be provided through the appropriate process.

I initially had a positive experience with TeamMoto and the salesperson Jesse, who was lovely throughout the sales process. I brought my family along when I came in to purchase my motorcycle and at the time I was extremely happy with the deal and experience,

Unfortunately the following morning I discovered that the conversation between myself and the business had been screenshot by said employee and forwarded to a toxic Facebook group. The groups name and content are inappropriate enough that I probably would get my review banned so I will not repeat it.

I was absolutely heartbroken, embarrassed and devastated by what had happened. I contacted the dealership and spoke with a manager who was polite and apologetic and I was told the matter would be handled. I was also offered compensation in recognition for what had happened

I then communicated with the dealership further and was led to believe I was being offered assistance following the breach of trust only to ultimately be directed to purchase items at marked price with around $30 taken off the helmet when I started to get upset at this point it was just a rouse to get me to spend more money
What should have been a straightforward one-day motorcycle purchase turned into days of phone calls, emails and frustration. I still have not received a response to my emails

I would strongly recommend being careful about what you communicate with the dealership electronically, as I never expected a private customer business conversation to end up being shared publicly.

Very disappointing experience. I want the one star I left on this review back.

one_star_reviews.text:
A word of caution for anyone considering building with Henley Homes – our experience.

I wanted to share our experience so others can ask the right questions before signing anything.

We initially signed with Carlisle and paid a $6,000 deposit. Although cancelling with Carlisle meant losing that money, we decided to move to Henley because we genuinely loved the Halcyon floor plan and believed the process would be more transparent.

Unfortunately, our experience turned out to be the complete opposite.

At our first meeting on 26 June, we made it very clear that we wanted the Imperial facade. We were told that the siting couldn't be completed on the Imperial facade because it was a new facade and the engineering drawings were not yet available. We were assured that by the time we signed the sales quotation, the engineering drawings would be ready and the house would be sited on the Imperial facade. Based on those assurances, we paid the initial $1,500 to proceed.

A month later, at our sales quotation appointment, there was no discussion about the siting at all. Instead, we felt rushed through the paperwork. I specifically asked for the documents to be emailed through DocuSign so we could read everything carefully before signing. We were told that creating a DocuSign would take too long and that if we delayed signing, our colour appointment and other appointments could be pushed back by another four weeks because our land title was approaching. Feeling pressured by the timeframes, we signed the paperwork on the spot.

While signing, I noticed the site costs had increased and questioned why. I was told the increase was due to the selected facade.

Only then did we realise the siting had changed significantly. The backyard had been reduced to around 2 metres, the house had been pushed much further back on the block, resulting in approximately a 7-metre driveway, and there was also a further 200 mm reduction from the porch, impacting the balcony as well. We were later told this related to building code/NCC requirements affecting Henley's balcony facades.

We then paid a further $500, and two days later our Project Administrator was assigned.

When our documents were uploaded to the Henley portal, we noticed the signed sales quotation had been uploaded, but the siting page was missing. When we raised our concerns with our Project Administrator, we were told to speak with the sales consultant as they couldn't assist.

We then contacted the sales manager, hoping to resolve the issue. Unfortunately, that conversation left us feeling blamed for the situation rather than supported.

At that point, we decided to cancel and sent through our cancellation request.

Afterwards, the manager contacted us offering the option of changing to another facade. However, we were told we would need to pay extra for that alternative. We explained that we had chosen Henley specifically for the Imperial facade and had proceeded based on the earlier assurances. Since the siting issue was not something we had created, we felt it would have been reasonable for Henley to offer an alternative facade as a goodwill solution rather than asking us to pay even more.

Ultimately, we were informed that they couldn't accommodate us and that cancelling would be the best option.

This was a very disappointing experience, especially after walking away from another builder and losing a significant deposit because we believed Henley would deliver a more transparent process.

I'm sharing this simply so others can be extra careful. My advice is:

- Read every page before signing.
- Ask for all siting documents upfront.
- Don't feel pressured into signing on the day.
- Make sure every promise is confirmed in writing.

This is our personal experience, and others may have different ones. I hope sharing it helps someone else avoid the stress, financial loss and disappointment that we went through.

Our sales consultant was Linda. Extremely unprofessional, impatient, unfriendly and absolutely unreliable!

Very disappointing customer service and communication

I took my vehicle in on 3 August for an audio repair that is covered under warranty. I was advised by Julie La Feria, the service advisor, that someone would be in contact with me regarding the repair.

Since last Wednesday, I have been trying to contact Julie to simply find out what is happening with my vehicle, but I have received no clear response or update.

My audio replacement is under warranty, and I am not asking for anything unreasonable. All I want to know is whether the required parts have arrived and when the repair is likely to be completed.

It is extremely frustrating to have to keep chasing a dealership for such a basic update. Good customer service should include keeping customers informed, especially when their vehicle has been sitting with you for a warranty repair.

If this is how you treat your customers after they have purchased a vehicle from you, then it is very disappointing and certainly not the level of customer service I expected.

I hope someone actually takes the time to respond and provide a proper update instead of leaving customers to repeatedly chase for information.

Being deliberately targeted with that kind of silent, hostile treatment while witnessing them be perfectly nice to the next customer is completely unacceptable and feels discriminatory.
